name: St. Regis New York
positioning: The St. Regis New York, founded in 1904 by John Jacob Astor IV, at Fifth Avenue and 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan; a New York City Landmark and home of the King Cole Bar
best_for: Travelers who want a historic Fifth Avenue base near Central Park and MoMA
Guests who value personal butler service

facts.text: The hotel is at Fifth Avenue and 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, steps from Central Park, Fifth Avenue shopping, MoMA and Rockefeller Center.
John Jacob Astor IV founded The St. Regis New York in 1904.
The hotel was declared a New York City Landmark in 1988.
The King Cole Bar is the home of the original Bloody Mary.
In 1934 bartender Fernand Petiot introduced the Red Snapper, which was later renamed the Bloody Mary.
The Drawing Room, formerly Astor Court, is a lounge-style space next to the King Cole Bar serving sharable bites and large plates.
La Maisonette draws inspiration from the hotel's original 1910s breakfast room.
Afternoon tea is served in La Maisonette.
Rooms keep original elements such as crystal Waterford chandeliers and crown moldings.
The hotel offers two-bedroom St. Regis, Grand and Milano suites.
The hotel has a rooftop ballroom with city views.
Bathrooms have bath amenities from Laboratoire Remede.

highlights.text: The Old King Cole mural in the King Cole Bar was painted by Maxfield Parrish in 1906 for the Knickerbocker hotel on 42nd Street.
The hotel has designer suites including the Dior Suite and the Bentley Suite, each inspired by a luxury brand.
Guests are looked after by a personal St. Regis butler during their stay.
The afternoon tea ritual dates back to Caroline Astor, matriarch of St. Regis.
The Caroline Astor Suite overlooks Central Park.

considerations.text: Valet parking is not available on Parade Days.
The hotel does not provide an airport shuttle service.
WhataHotel notes a busy Midtown location with heavy foot traffic.
